associations.rationale: This counts an auxiliary index type for the principal family; the source theorem does not state this cardinality, so it is supporting classification infrastructure.
The character formula for the one-dimensional determinant representation helps identify the summand C_mu but is not one of the theorem's three displayed assertions.
The fact that the determinant-character representation has dimension one supports the decomposition in part (2), but the source's asserted q-dimensional object is W_mu.
This classifies isomorphisms among the auxiliary determinant characters, whereas part (3) classifies the W_mu and unequal-character principal series.
Simplicity of the one-dimensional determinant character is a prerequisite used around the direct-sum decomposition, not the theorem's asserted simplicity of W_mu or of unequal principal series.
This existentially packages a simple pairwise-nonisomorphic family and its size; it is a derived aggregate classification statement rather than any displayed part of Theorem 5.25.2.
This merely constructs the indexed principal family and makes no theorem-level irreducibility, decomposition, or isomorphism assertion.
Injectivity of the opaque aggregate family is a packaged consequence of the source's isomorphism classifications, not their direct lambda-parameter statement.
Simplicity of every member of the aggregate principalFamily combines cases behind an opaque index, so it supports rather than directly states parts (1) and (2).
The q+1 dimension of a principal-series representation is useful for the decomposition and q-dimensional complement, but it is not itself a displayed assertion of the theorem.
The type states only part (1), not the decomposition and isomorphism classifications in parts (2) and (3).
The type states only part (2), not the irreducibility and isomorphism assertions in parts (1) and (3).
The type states only the first isomorphism assertion of part (3), not the other numbered conclusions of the theorem.
The type states only the second isomorphism assertion of part (3), not the theorem's irreducibility, decomposition, and first isomorphism conclusions.
